GUILFORD, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Hyperfine, Inc. (Nasdaq: HYPR), the groundbreaking health technology company that has redefined brain imaging with the first FDA-cleared AI-powered portable MRI system for the brain—the Swoop® system—today announced that management will present at the Piper Sandler 38th Annual Healthcare Conference in New York on Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 9:10 a.m. Eastern Time. Management will also host in-person investor meetings at the conference.

A live webcast, as well as an archived recording, will be available on the “Investors” section of the Company’s website at: https://investors.hyperfine.io/. The webcast will be archived and available for replay for at least 90 days after the event.

To schedule a one-on-one meeting with Hyperfine management, please reach out to your Piper Sandler representative, or the investor contact below.

About the Swoop® Portable MRI Systems

The Swoop® Portable MR Imaging® Systems are U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared for brain imaging of patients of all ages. They are portable, ultra-low-field magnetic resonance imaging devices for producing images that display the internal structure of the head where full diagnostic examination is not clinically practical. When interpreted by a trained physician, these images provide information that can be useful in determining a diagnosis.

About Hyperfine, Inc.

Hyperfine, Inc. (Nasdaq: HYPR) is the groundbreaking health technology company that has redefined brain imaging with the Swoop® system—the first FDA-cleared, portable, ultra-low-field, magnetic resonance brain imaging system capable of providing imaging at multiple points of professional care. The mission of Hyperfine, Inc. is to revolutionize patient care globally through transformational, accessible, clinically relevant diagnostic imaging. Founded by Dr. Jonathan Rothberg in a technology-based incubator called 4Catalyzer, Hyperfine, Inc. scientists, engineers, and physicists developed the Swoop® system out of a passion for redefining brain imaging methodology and how clinicians can apply accessible diagnostic imaging to patient care. For more information, visit HyperfineMRI.com.

PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Guardant Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: GH), a leading precision oncology company, today announced the U.S. clinical launch of Guardant Reveal® Ultra, a new molecular residual disease (MRD) platform for solid tumors offering personalized, ultra-sensitive detection of residual cancer. Built on Guardant’s Smart Platform, Reveal Ultra incorporates tumor-informed, patient-specific genomic alterations to provide one of the most advanced and actionable views of MRD.

Validated on thousands of clinical samples, Guardant Reveal Ultra has demonstrated detection sensitivity of 1 part per million (ppm) or below across major tumor types. The test incorporates patient-specific alterations from thousands of genomic targets spanning all major variant classes, including structural variants. Guardant Reveal Ultra has also been validated with tissue samples containing as little as 5% tumor cellularity, significantly below the typical industry requirement of 20%, enabling testing across a broader range of clinical specimens.

“Reveal Ultra opens a new frontier in MRD detection,” said Helmy Eltoukhy, Guardant Health chairman and co-CEO. “While detecting cancer at one part per million has become an important benchmark, what truly matters is delivering that level of sensitivity reliably across real clinical samples and a broad range of tumor types. Reveal Ultra was built to meet that challenge, bringing extraordinary precision to everyday clinical practice and advancing our ability to track and manage each patient’s cancer throughout their journey.”

Guardant Reveal Ultra is designed as a connected experience, enabling physicians the option of a direct path from MRD detection to clinical action through Guardant360® Liquid. Together with Guardant Reveal®’s best-in-class tissue-free MRD detection and therapy monitoring capabilities, and Guardant360 Liquid and Guardant360® Tissue for comprehensive genomic profiling, Guardant Reveal Ultra completes Guardant’s precision oncology portfolio. These solutions work hand-in-hand to support physicians in selecting therapies, monitoring treatment response, detecting residual disease, and managing cancer throughout the patient journey.

About Guardant Health

Guardant Health is a leading precision oncology company focused on guarding wellness and giving every person more time free from cancer. Founded in 2012, Guardant is transforming patient care and accelerating new cancer therapies by providing critical insights into what drives disease through its advanced blood and tissue tests, real-world data and AI analytics. Guardant tests help improve outcomes across all stages of care, including screening to find cancer early, monitoring for recurrence in early-stage cancer, and treatment selection for patients with advanced cancer. For more information, visit guardanthealth.com and follow the company on LinkedIn, X (Twitter) and Facebook.

Key Terms

molecular residual diseasemedical
Molecular residual disease is the tiny amount of cancer that can remain in the body after treatment and is detectable only by sensitive tests that find cancer DNA or other molecular traces. It matters to investors because these measurements can predict relapse, guide whether additional therapy is needed, and shape the market for diagnostics and drugs—much like finding embers after a fire helps decide if more firefighting is required.
structural variantstechnical
Structural variants are large-scale changes in an organism’s DNA—such as missing, extra, flipped, or rearranged chunks of genetic material—that are like tearing out, duplicating, or reshuffling chapters in a book. Investors should care because these changes can drive or explain diseases, alter how well diagnostics and therapies work, and shift the commercial and regulatory outlook for drugs, tests, and gene-based treatments.
tumor cellularitymedical
The proportion of a tissue sample that is made up of actual tumor (malignant) cells rather than non-malignant components such as stroma, inflammatory cells, blood, or necrotic debris; expressed as a percentage of tumor cells among the nucleated cells in the specimen. Tumor cellularity is assessed by a pathologist on the biopsy or surgical specimen and affects how reliable molecular tests (like DNA sequencing or biomarker assays) are because low cellularity can dilute tumor-derived signals; it can also vary within and between samples due to tumor heterogeneity and sampling or processing factors.

LADERA RANCH, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Strategic Storage Trust VI, Inc. (“SST VI”), a publicly registered non-traded real estate investment trust sponsored by an affiliate of SmartStop Self Storage REIT, Inc. (“SmartStop”) (NYSE: SMA), announced operating results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

“This quarter demonstrated the resilience of our operating platform and the progress we are making across our portfolio,” said H. Michael Schwartz, President and Chief Executive Officer of SST VI. “We grew total revenues 1.8% for the quarter and 4.3% year to date, and same-store rent per occupied square foot rose 2.7% through the first nine months. While same-store results reflected near-term pressure this quarter, our development and joint venture properties continued to advance, with new openings in Ontario and Bradenton providing opportunities for future growth.

“Subsequent to quarter end, we completed our merger with Strategic Storage Growth Trust III, an important milestone that creates a billion-dollar self-storage REIT with 37 wholly-owned facilities across ten states and three Canadian provinces, including our entry into California, New Jersey and Texas. With general and administrative costs essentially flat year to date, we believe spreading our corporate costs across a portfolio nearly 50% larger will meaningfully improve our operating efficiency and create a stronger, more agile company. As we move into 2027, we look forward to the first full year of contribution from our combined portfolio, continued lease-up across our Canadian joint ventures and Bradenton properties, and a development pipeline that now includes two additional joint venture projects in British Columbia and Québec. We believe these initiatives position SST VI to drive long-term value for our stockholders.”

Key Highlights for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026:

  • Total revenues were approximately $8.1 million, an increase of approximately $0.1 million compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Same-store revenues decreased by 0.9% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Net loss attributable to common stockholders decreased approximately $0.3 million or 2.8% compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Decreased same-store Net Operating Income (“NOI”) by 5.6% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Key Highlights for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026:

  • Total revenues were approximately $23.9 million, an increase of approximately $1.0 million compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Increased Same-store revenues by 1.6% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Net loss attributable to common stockholder increased by approximately $8.4 million or 30.5% compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Decreased same-store NOI by 1.9% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

SSGT III Merger:

On November 1, 2026, we closed on our merger (the “SSGT III Merger”) with Strategic Storage Growth Trust III, Inc. (“SSGT III”).

As a result of the SSGT III Merger, we acquired all of the real estate owned by SSGT III, which as of the closing date of the SSGT III Merger consisted of (i) 12 wholly-owned self storage facilities located in four states and three Canadian provinces comprising approximately 9,215 self storage units and approximately 981,465 net rentable square feet, (ii) SSGT III’s 50% equity interest in three unconsolidated real estate ventures located in two Canadian provinces (British Columbia and Quebec), and (iii) beneficial interests in three Delaware Statutory Trust (“DST”) sponsored programs that own eight properties, consisting of approximately 5,370 units and nearly 0.7 million net rentable square feet. The unconsolidated real estate ventures consist of one operating self storage property and two parcels of land being developed into self storage facilities, with subsidiaries of SmartCentres owning the other 50% of such entities.

As a result of the SSGT III Merger, approximately 17.4 million shares of our Class A common stock were issued in exchange for approximately 17.4 million shares of SSGT III common stock.

Concurrently with the SSGT III Merger, SSGT III, SSGT III’s operating partnership, and SSGT III’s external advisor, an affiliate of SmartStop, terminated SSGT III’s advisory agreement. In accordance with such termination, immediately prior to the Merger Effective Time, SSGT III’s advisor received $2.0 million in units of limited partnership interests in SSGT III’s operating partnership, which represented the agreed amount payable to SSGT III’s advisor, notwithstanding the disposition fee and related calculations due under SSGT III’s advisory agreement. As a result of the SSGT III Merger, approximately 0.7 million units of limited partnership interest in our operating partnership were issued in exchange for approximately 0.7 million units of limited partnership interest in SSGT III’s operating partnership.

Development Projects:

On November 3, 2026, we substantially completed development and commenced operations on a parcel of land adjacent to our Bradenton property consisting of an additional approximately 280 units and 29,900 net rentable square feet.

Declared Distributions:

On September 30, 2026, our board of directors declared a daily distribution rate of approximately $0.001698 per day per share on the outstanding shares of common stock payable to Class P, Class A, Class T, Class W, Class Y and Class Z stockholders of record of such shares as shown on our books at the close of business on each day of the period commencing on October 1, 2026 and ending December 31, 2026. In connection with this distribution, stockholders who hold Class T and Class Y shares will be paid an amount equal to approximately $0.001698 per day less the stockholder servicing fee payable per share per day. Such distributions payable to each stockholder of record during a month will be paid the following month.

About Strategic Storage Trust VI, Inc. (SST VI):

SST VI is a public non-traded REIT that invests in income-producing and growth self-storage facilities in the United States and Canada. As of November 19, 2026, SST VI owned 37 wholly-owned operating self-storage properties in ten states and three Canadian provinces, comprising approximately 29,400 units and 3.2 million rentable square feet, in addition to joint venture interests in six operating and two developmental properties in three Canadian provinces (British Columbia, Ontario and Québec), and beneficial interests in three DST programs that own eight properties consisting of approximately 5,370 units and nearly 0.7 million net rentable square feet.

About SmartStop Self Storage REIT, Inc. (SmartStop):

SmartStop (NYSE: SMA) is a self-managed REIT with a fully integrated operations team of more than 1,000 self-storage professionals focused on growing the SmartStop® Self Storage brand. SmartStop, through its indirect subsidiary SmartStop REIT Advisors, LLC, also sponsors other self-storage programs, and through its Managed Platform offers third-party management services in the U.S. and Canada. Net operating income, or NOI, is a non-GAAP measure that we define as net income (loss), computed in accordance with GAAP, generated from properties before corporate general and administrative expenses, asset management fees, interest expense, depreciation, amortization, acquisition expenses, tenant protection economics, and other non-property related income and expense. We believe that NOI is useful for investors as it provides a measure of the operating performance of our operating assets because NOI excludes certain items that are not associated with the ongoing operation of the properties. Additionally, we believe that NOI (sometimes referred to as property operating income) is a widely accepted measure of comparative operating performance in the real estate community. However, our use of the term NOI may not be comparable to that of other real estate companies as they may have different methodologies for computing this amount. In addition, NOI is not a substitute for net income (loss), cash flows from operations, or other related financial measures, in evaluating our operating performance.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - New Zealand Energy Corp. (TSXV: NZ) ("NZEC" or the "Company") is pleased to announce a non-brokered private placement (the "Offering") for gross proceeds of up to C$3,000,000, the commencement of its planned oil well workover campaign, and continued solid production from the Tariki 1A well.

Private Placement

The Company intends to complete the Offering of common shares of the Company (each, a "Common Share") at a price of C$0.35 per Common Share for aggregate gross proceeds of up to C$3,000,000.

The net proceeds of the Offering are expected to be used to ensure the Company has sufficient working capital to undertake operations on the Tariki Gas Storage Project, to fund the Company's share of active oil well interventions, to bring the Tariki 5A well onto long-term production, and for general working capital purposes.

The Company is also preparing to order long lead items related to the gas storage project and is working to secure a significant lending package to support the funding of the development costs. In connection with the anticipated capital facility, the Company intends to ensure it has sufficient working capital to carry the Tariki Gas Storage Project through to a final investment decision.

The Offering is expected to close on or about November 30, 2026. Closing of the Offering is subject to the receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals, including the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV"). All Common Shares issued pursuant to the Offering will be subject to a hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws and the policies of the TSXV. The Company may pay finders' fees in connection with the Offering.

Oil Operations

NZEC expects to commence its planned oil well workover campaign shortly. Over the next few months, the Company expects to add over 800 barrels of oil per day (gross) of production through well clean-outs, additional perforations, and pump additions on its Ngaere and Waihapa wells.

In addition, working with the Company's joint venture partner, Monumental Energy Corp. (TSXV: MNRG), the Company has received promising initial laboratory results using flow assurance chemicals, and a pilot trial will be undertaken at Copper Moki to test the potential uplift in production.

Tariki Production

The Tariki 1A well continues to deliver consistent stabilized flow rates of approximately 2.5 MMcf/d (gross) and has been dewatering the Tariki reservoir at approximately 1,600 barrels of water per day. The well forms part of Petroleum Mining Licence PML 38138, in which NZEC holds a 50% interest. The Company's activities at Tariki are conducted together with its co-venturer, L&M Energy Limited.

NZEC continues to focus on optimizing production through debottlenecking work at its Waihapa production station and is evaluating providing third-party access to several groups, subject to the success of their exploration activities.

Toby Pierce, Chief Executive Officer of NZEC, commented: "We continue to methodically advance the gas storage project and remain in active commercial discussions to both fund and build the project in due course. Further, given the elevated Brent oil prices at the moment, advancing our oil production is a key growth driver for the Company."

NZEC is a publicly listed energy company focused on the development of oil, gas, and gas-storage opportunities in New Zealand. The Company holds interests in multiple heritage assets and development-stage projects, including the Tariki Gas Storage Project in Taranaki. ST. LOUIS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Post Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: POST), a consumer packaged goods holding company, today reported results for the fourth fiscal quarter and fiscal year ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights:

  • Fourth quarter net sales of $2.0 billion; operating profit of $205.1 million; net earnings of $81.8 million and Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)* of $378.4 million
  • Fiscal year net sales of $8.1 billion; operating profit of $837.6 million; net earnings of $316.6 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $1,568.9 million
  • Fiscal year 2027 Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)* expected to range between $1,450-$1,500 million

*For additional information regarding non-GAAP measures, such as Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted net earnings, Adjusted diluted earnings per common share and segment Adjusted EBITDA, see the related explanations presented under "Use of Non-GAAP Measures" later in this release. Post provides Adjusted EBITDA guidance only on a non-GAAP basis and does not provide a reconciliation of its forward-looking Adjusted EBITDA non-GAAP guidance measure to the most directly comparable GAAP measure due to the inherent difficulty in forecasting and quantifying certain amounts that are necessary for such reconciliation, including the adjustments described under "Outlook" below.

Basis of Presentation

On May 1, 2026, Post completed its sale of substantially all of the assets of Crystal Farms Dairy Company (the "Crystal Farms Business"), the results of which were reported in the Refrigerated Retail segment prior to the sale. On December 1, 2025, Post completed its sale of the pasta business of 8th Avenue Food & Provisions, Inc. ("8th Avenue"); its operating results prior to the sale were reported in the Post Consumer Brands segment.

Certain prior-period amounts presented herein have been revised to reflect the correction of an immaterial error related to the timing of recognition of stock-based compensation expense. Previously reported Adjusted EBITDA, segment profit and free cash flow were not impacted by the revision. See Notes 2 and 22 to the consolidated financial statements included in Post's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2026, expected to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on or around November 19, 2026, for additional information.

Fourth Quarter Consolidated Operating Results

Net sales were $1,954.5 million, a decrease of 13.0%, or $292.5 million, compared to $2,247.0 million in the prior year period which included $138.5 million in net sales from divestitures. Excluding contributions from divestitures in the prior year period, net sales declined across Foodservice (driven by the lapping of avian influenza driven pricing in the prior year) and Post Consumer Brands (driven by pet food and value cereal volume declines), while Refrigerated Retail and Weetabix net sales were approximately flat. Gross profit was $566.6 million, or 29.0% of net sales, a decrease of 5.9%, or $35.5 million, compared to $602.1 million, or 26.8% of net sales, in the prior year period.

Selling, general and administrative ("SG&A") expenses were $309.3 million, or 15.8% of net sales, a decrease of 9.9%, or $34.0 million, compared to $343.3 million, or 15.3% of net sales, in the prior year period. The decrease in SG&A in the current year period was primarily driven by the absence of divested businesses and lower incentive compensation, partially offset by a $6.0 million accrual for litigation expense related to Post's Refrigerated Retail segment. Operating profit was $205.1 million, an increase of 17.1%, or $29.9 million, compared to $175.2 million in the prior year period. Operating profit in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 included a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $29.8 million, which is discussed later in this release and was treated as an adjustment for non-GAAP measures.

Net earnings were $81.8 million, an increase of 41.0%, or $23.8 million, compared to $58.0 million in the prior year period.

Diluted earnings per common share were $1.68, compared to $0.99 in the prior year period. Adjusted net earnings (non-GAAP)* were $92.6 million, compared to $134.5 million in the prior year period. Adjusted diluted earnings per common share (non-GAAP)* were $1.84, compared to $2.20 in the prior year period.

Adjusted EBITDA was $378.4 million, a decrease of 11.0%, or $47.0 million, compared to $425.4 million in the prior year period.

Fiscal Year 2026 Consolidated Operating Results

Net sales were $8,120.0 million, a decrease of 0.5%, or $38.1 million, compared to $8,158.1 million in the prior year. Gross profit was $2,389.0 million, or 29.4% of net sales, an increase of 2.1%, or $49.6 million, compared to $2,339.4 million, or 28.7% of net sales, in the prior year.

SG&A expenses were $1,326.0 million, or 16.3% of net sales, an increase of 1.2%, or $15.8 million, compared to $1,310.2 million, or 16.1% of net sales, in the prior year. Operating profit was $837.6 million, an increase of 5.0%, or $39.9 million, compared to $797.7 million in the prior year.

Net earnings were $316.6 million, a decrease of 5.4%, or $18.0 million, compared to $334.6 million in the prior year. Net earnings included the following:

Post Consumer Brands

Primarily North American ready-to-eat ("RTE") cereal and granola, pet food and nut butters.

For the fourth quarter, net sales were $989.6 million, a decrease of 14.6%, or $169.2 million, compared to the prior year period. Net sales included $100.2 million in the fourth fiscal quarter of 2025 attributable to the divested pasta business. Excluding the benefit of the pasta business in the prior year period, volumes decreased 9.9% as pet food volumes declined 12.7% and cereal and granola volumes declined 4.4%. Pet food volume losses were primarily driven by distribution losses and category declines. Cereal and granola volume losses were primarily driven by category declines, distribution losses in value cereal and branded assortment changes. Segment profit was $149.7 million, an increase of 45.6%, or $46.9 million, compared to the prior year period. Segment Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)* was $215.4 million, an increase of 3.6%, or $7.4 million, compared to the prior year period.

For fiscal year 2026, net sales were $4,112.5 million, an increase of 2.2%, or $87.9 million, compared to the prior year. Segment profit was $543.3 million, an increase of 10.0%, or $49.4 million, compared to the prior year. Segment Adjusted EBITDA was $816.2 million, an increase of 2.8%, or $22.1 million, compared to the prior year.

Foodservice

Primarily egg and potato products.

For the fourth quarter, net sales were $635.2 million, a decrease of 11.5%, or $82.8 million, compared to the prior year period. Volumes decreased 2.6%, driven primarily by the lapping of customer egg inventory replenishment in the prior year. Segment profit was $91.2 million, a decrease of 28.9%, or $37.0 million, compared to the prior year period. Segment Adjusted EBITDA was $121.6 million, a decrease of 24.5%, or $39.5 million, compared to the prior year period. Declines in net sales, segment profit and segment Adjusted EBITDA reflect the lapping of avian influenza pricing in the prior year period.

For fiscal year 2026, net sales were $2,584.6 million, a decrease of 2.1%, or $56.4 million, compared to the prior year. Segment profit was $419.3 million, an increase of 4.9%, or $19.6 million, compared to the prior year. Segment Adjusted EBITDA was $556.8 million, an increase of 4.5%, or $23.9 million, compared to the prior year.

Refrigerated Retail

Primarily side dish, egg and sausage products.

For the fourth quarter, net sales were $187.4 million, a decrease of 17.9%, or $40.8 million, compared to the prior year period. Net sales included $38.3 million in the fourth fiscal quarter of 2025 related to the Crystal Farms Business. Excluding the contribution from the Crystal Farms Business, volumes increased 2.3%, primarily due to an increase in side dish products driven by the introduction of private label offerings. Volume information by product is disclosed in a table presented later in this release. Segment profit was $12.2 million, a decrease of 47.9%, or $11.2 million, compared to the prior year period, and reflected a $6.0 million accrual for litigation expense. Segment Adjusted EBITDA was $29.4 million, a decrease of 35.5%, or $16.2 million, compared to the prior year period. Declines in net sales, segment profit and segment Adjusted EBITDA primarily reflect the divestiture of the Crystal Farms Business in the current year period and the lapping of avian influenza pricing in the prior year period.

For fiscal year 2026, net sales were $873.8 million, a decrease of 8.3%, or $79.5 million, compared to the prior year. Segment profit was $74.2 million, a decrease of 16.0%, or $14.1 million, compared to the prior year. Segment Adjusted EBITDA was $146.9 million, a decrease of 12.1%, or $20.3 million, compared to the prior year.

Weetabix

Primarily United Kingdom RTE cereal, muesli and protein-based shakes.

For the fourth quarter, net sales were $143.1 million, a decrease of 1.3%, or $1.9 million, compared to the prior year period. Net sales reflected a foreign currency exchange rate tailwind of approximately 30 basis points. Volumes decreased 0.6%, as declines in private label products were partially offset by growth in branded products. Segment profit was $24.2 million, an increase of 17.5%, or $3.6 million, compared to the prior year period. Segment Adjusted EBITDA was $35.4 million, an increase of 8.6%, or $2.8 million, compared to the prior year period.

For fiscal year 2026, net sales were $554.2 million, an increase of 2.2%, or $12.0 million, compared to the prior year. Segment profit was $92.8 million, an increase of 25.4%, or $18.8 million, compared to the prior year. Segment Adjusted EBITDA was $138.1 million, an increase of 11.6%, or $14.4 million, compared to the prior year.

Impairment of Goodwill

A non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $29.8 million was recorded in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 related to Post's Cheese and Dairy reporting unit within the Refrigerated Retail segment, which has since been divested. No goodwill impairment charge was recorded in fiscal year 2026.

Interest, Loss on Extinguishment of Debt, (Income) Expense on Swaps and Income Tax

Interest expense, net was $107.4 million and $424.7 million in the three months and fiscal year ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $101.8 million and $361.4 million in the three months and fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The increase in interest expense, net in the current year periods was driven by higher average outstanding principal amounts of debt, a higher weighted-average interest rate and lower interest income compared to the prior year periods.

There was no gain or loss on extinguishment of debt in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 or 2025. Loss on extinguishment of debt, net of $17.5 million was recorded in fiscal year 2026 in connection with Post's redemption of its 5.50% senior notes due December 2029. Loss on extinguishment of debt, net of $5.8 million was recorded in fiscal year 2025 in connection with Post's redemption of its 5.625% senior notes due January 2028.

(Income) expense on swaps, net relates to mark-to-market adjustments on interest rate swaps. Income on swaps, net was $14.0 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 compared to an expense of $0.4 million in the prior year period. Income on swaps, net was $20.9 million in fiscal year 2026 compared to $6.9 million in the prior year.

Income tax expense was $32.1 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, an effective income tax rate of 28.2%, compared to $21.7 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, an effective income tax rate of 27.2%. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the effective income tax rate differed significantly from the statutory tax rate primarily as a result of valuation allowances on certain state attributes. For the three months ended September 30, 2025, the effective income tax rate differed significantly from the statutory tax rate primarily as a result of a non-deductible goodwill impairment charge discussed previously in this release and the derecognition of basis differences attributable to 8th Avenue, partially offset by the release of a valuation allowance on one of Post's foreign operations. Income tax expense was $110.8 million in fiscal year 2026, an effective income tax rate of 25.9%, compared to $108.2 million in the prior year, an effective income tax rate of 24.5%.

Share Repurchases

During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, Post repurchased 1.2 million shares of its common stock for $100.3 million at an average price of $83.51 per share. During fiscal year 2026, Post repurchased 10.3 million shares for $1,009.1 million at an average price of $98.37 per share. Subsequent to the end of the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 through November 16, 2026, Post repurchased 0.4 million shares for $33.0 million at an average price of $79.06 per share. As of November 16, 2026, Post had $396.7 million remaining under its share repurchase authorization.

Outlook

Post management expects Adjusted EBITDA for fiscal year 2027 to be between $1,450-$1,500 million. Post management expects fiscal year 2027 capital expenditures to range between $360-$400 million, which includes continued Foodservice investment in cage-free egg facility expansion and Post Consumer Brands investment in nut butter manufacturing optimization.

Post provides Adjusted EBITDA guidance only on a non-GAAP basis and does not provide a reconciliation of its forward-looking Adjusted EBITDA non-GAAP guidance measure to the most directly comparable GAAP measure due to the inherent difficulty in forecasting and quantifying certain amounts that are necessary for such reconciliation, including adjustments that could be made for income/expense on swaps, net, integration and transaction costs, mark-to-market adjustments on equity security investments, mark-to-market adjustments on commodity and foreign exchange hedges, gain/loss on extinguishment of debt, net, equity method investment adjustment and other items reflected in Post's reconciliations of historical numbers, the amounts of which, based on historical experience, could be significant. For additional information regarding Post's non-GAAP measures, see the related explanations presented under "Use of Non-GAAP Measures."

Use of Non-GAAP Measures

Post uses certain non-GAAP measures in this release to supplement the financial measures prepared in accordance with United States ("U.S.") generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP"). These non-GAAP measures include Adjusted net earnings/loss, Adjusted diluted earnings/loss per common share, Adjusted EBITDA, segment Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Net Sales, segment Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Net Sales, free cash flow, net leverage as calculated under Post's credit agreement and consolidated interest coverage ratio as calculated under Post's credit agreement. The reconciliation of each of these non-GAAP measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measure is provided later in this release under "Explanation and Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures."

Management uses certain of these non-GAAP measures, including Adjusted EBITDA and segment Adjusted EBITDA, as key metrics in the evaluation of underlying company and segment performance, in making financial, operating and planning decisions and, in part, in the determination of bonuses for its executive officers and employees. Additionally, Post is required to comply with certain covenants and limitations that are based on variations of EBITDA in its financing documents. Management believes the use of these non-GAAP measures provides increased transparency and assists investors in understanding the underlying operating performance of Post and its segments and in the analysis of ongoing operating trends. Non-GAAP measures are not prepared in accordance with GAAP, as they exclude certain items as described later in this release. These non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies. For additional information regarding Post's non-GAAP measures, see the related explanations provided under "Explanation and Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures."

EXPLANATION AND RECONCILIATION OF NON-GAAP MEASURES

Post uses certain non-GAAP measures in this release to supplement the financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. These non-GAAP measures include Adjusted net earnings/loss, Adjusted diluted earnings/loss per common share, Adjusted EBITDA, segment Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Net Sales, segment Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Net Sales, free cash flow, net leverage as calculated under Post's credit agreement and consolidated interest coverage ratio as calculated under Post's credit agreement. The reconciliation of each of these non-GAAP measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measure is provided in the tables following this section. Non-GAAP measures are not prepared in accordance with GAAP, as they exclude certain items as described below. These non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies.

Adjusted net earnings/loss and Adjusted diluted earnings/loss per common share
Post believes Adjusted net earnings/loss and Adjusted diluted earnings/loss per common share are useful to investors in evaluating Post's operating performance because they exclude items that affect the comparability of Post's financial results and could potentially distort an understanding of the trends in business performance.

Adjusted net earnings/loss and Adjusted diluted earnings/loss per common share are adjusted for the following items:

a.

Loss on amounts held for sale: Post has excluded losses recorded to adjust the carrying value of businesses, facilities and other assets and liabilities classified as held for sale as the amount and frequency of such adjustments are not consistent. Additionally, Post believes that these losses do not reflect expected ongoing future operating expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

b.

Restructuring and facility closure costs, including accelerated depreciation, net: Post has excluded certain costs associated with facility closures and the gains and losses recorded on the sales of such facilities as the amount and frequency of such adjustments are not consistent. Additionally, Post believes that these costs do not reflect expected ongoing future operating expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

c.

Income/expense on swaps, net: Post has excluded the impact of mark-to-market adjustments and cash settlements on interest rate swaps due to the inherent uncertainty and volatility associated with such amounts based on changes in assumptions with respect to estimates of fair value and economic conditions and as the amount and frequency of such adjustments are not consistent.

d.

Impairment of goodwill: Post has excluded expenses for impairment of Post's previous Cheese and Dairy reporting unit as such non-cash amounts are inconsistent in amount and frequency and Post believes that these costs do not reflect expected ongoing future operating expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

e.

Debt premiums paid/discounts received, net: Post has excluded payments and other expenses for premiums on debt extinguishment, net of gains realized on debt repurchased at a discount, as such payments are inconsistent in amount and frequency. Additionally, Post believes that these costs do not reflect expected ongoing future operating expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

f.

Inventory revaluation adjustment on acquired businesses: Post has excluded the impact of fair value step-up adjustments to inventory in connection with business combinations as such adjustments represent non-cash items, are not consistent in amount and frequency and are significantly impacted by the timing and size of Post's acquisitions.

g.

Integration costs and transaction costs: Post has excluded transaction costs related to professional service fees and other related costs associated with signed and closed business combinations and closed divestitures and integration costs incurred to integrate acquired or to-be-acquired businesses or assets as Post believes that these exclusions allow for more meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance and comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods. Post believes such costs are generally not relevant to assessing or estimating the long-term performance of acquired businesses or assets as part of Post or the performance of Post subsequent to the divestiture of the businesses or assets, and such costs are not factored into management's evaluation of potential acquisitions or Post's performance after completion of an acquisition or the evaluation to divest a business or asset. In addition, the frequency and amount of such charges varies significantly based on the size and timing of the transaction and the maturity of any businesses being acquired or divested. Also, the size, complexity and/or volume of past transactions, which often drive the magnitude of such expenses, may not be indicative of the size, complexity and/or volume of future transactions. By excluding these expenses, management is better able to evaluate Post's ability to utilize its existing assets and estimate the long-term value that acquired businesses or assets will generate for Post.

h.

Asset disposal costs: Post has excluded costs recorded in connection with the disposal of certain assets which were never put into use and/or the demolition and site remediation of unused facilities as the amount and frequency of these costs are not consistent. Additionally, Post believes that these costs do not reflect expected ongoing future operating expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

i.

Mark-to-market adjustments on commodity and foreign exchange hedges: Post has excluded the impact of mark-to-market adjustments on commodity and foreign exchange hedges due to the inherent uncertainty and volatility associated with such amounts based on changes in assumptions with respect to fair value estimates. Additionally, these adjustments are primarily non-cash items, and the amount and frequency of such adjustments are not consistent.

j.

Mark-to-market adjustments on equity security investments: Post has excluded the impact of mark-to-market adjustments on equity security investments due to the inherent volatility associated with such amounts based on changes in market pricing variations and as the amount and frequency of such adjustments are not consistent. Additionally, these adjustments are primarily non-cash items and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

k.

Gain/loss on sale of business: Post has excluded gains and losses recorded on divestitures as the amount and frequency of such amounts are not consistent. Additionally, Post believes that these gains and losses do not reflect expected ongoing future operating income and expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

l.

Provision for legal settlements: Post has excluded gains and losses recorded to recognize the anticipated or actual resolution of certain litigation as Post believes such gains and losses do not reflect expected ongoing future operating income and expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

m.

Costs expected to be indemnified, net: Post has excluded certain costs incurred and expected to be indemnified in connection with damaged assets and gains related to indemnification proceeds received above the carrying value of damaged assets as Post believes such gains and losses do not reflect expected ongoing future operating income and expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

n.

Advisory income: Post has excluded advisory income received from 8th Avenue prior to Post's acquisition of 8th Avenue as Post believes such income did not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

o.

Income tax effect on adjustments: Post has included the income tax impact of the non-GAAP adjustments using a rate described in the applicable footnote of the reconciliation tables to be consistent with the treatment of these adjustments in the calculation of the non-GAAP measure.

Adjusted EBITDA, segment Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Net Sales and segment Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Net Sales
Post believes that Adjusted EBITDA is useful to investors in evaluating Post's operating performance and liquidity because (i) Post believes it is widely used to measure a company's operating performance without regard to items such as depreciation and amortization, which can vary depending upon accounting methods and the book value of assets, (ii) it presents a measure of corporate performance exclusive of Post's capital structure and the method by which the assets were acquired and (iii) it is a financial indicator of a company's ability to service its debt, as Post is required to comply with certain covenants and limitations that are based on variations of EBITDA in its financing documents. Post believes that segment Adjusted EBITDA is useful to investors in evaluating Post's operating performance because it allows for assessment of the operating performance of each reportable segment. Management uses Adjusted EBITDA to provide forward-looking guidance and uses Adjusted EBITDA and segment Adjusted EBITDA to forecast future results. Post believes that Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Net Sales and segment Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of Net Sales are measures useful to investors in evaluating Post's operating performance because they allow for meaningful comparison of operating performance across periods.

Adjusted EBITDA and segment Adjusted EBITDA reflect adjustments for interest expense, net, income tax expense/benefit, and depreciation and amortization, and the following adjustments discussed above: loss on amounts held for sale, restructuring and facility closure costs, net, income/expense on swaps, net, impairment of goodwill, inventory revaluation adjustment on acquired businesses, integration costs and transaction costs, asset disposal costs, mark-to-market adjustments on commodity and foreign exchange hedges, mark-to-market adjustments on equity security investments, gain/loss on sale of business,  provision for legal settlements, costs expected to be indemnified, net and advisory income. Additionally, Adjusted EBITDA and segment Adjusted EBITDA reflect adjustments for the following items:

p.

Stock-based compensation: Post's compensation strategy includes the use of stock-based compensation to attract and retain executives and employees by aligning their long-term compensation interests with shareholders' investment interests. Post has excluded stock-based compensation as stock-based compensation can vary significantly based on reasons such as the timing, size and nature of the awards granted and subjective assumptions which are unrelated to operational decisions and performance in any particular period and does not contribute to meaningful comparisons of Post's operating performances to other periods.

q.

Gain/loss on extinguishment of debt, net: Post has excluded gains and losses recorded on extinguishment of debt, inclusive of payments for premiums and tender fees and the write-off of debt issuance costs, net of gains realized on the write-off of unamortized debt premiums and debt repurchased at a discount, as such gains and losses are inconsistent in amount and frequency. Additionally, Post believes that these gains and losses do not reflect expected ongoing future operating income and expenses and do not contribute to a meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance or comparisons of Post's operating performance to other periods.

r.

Equity method investment adjustment: Post has included adjustments for its portion of income tax expense/benefit, interest expense, net and depreciation and amortization for Weetabix's unconsolidated investment accounted for using equity method accounting as Post believes these adjustments contribute to a more meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance.

s.

Noncontrolling interest adjustment: Post has included adjustments for income tax expense/benefit, interest expense, net and depreciation and amortization for Weetabix's consolidated investment which is attributable to the noncontrolling owners of Weetabix's consolidated investment as Post believes these adjustments contribute to a more meaningful evaluation of Post's current operating performance.

Free cash flow
Free cash flow is a non-GAAP measure which represents net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditures. Post believes free cash flow is useful to investors in evaluating Post's ability to service debt and repurchase shares of its common stock.

Net leverage as calculated under Post's credit agreement
Net leverage as calculated under Post's credit agreement is a non-GAAP measure which represents total principal debt less cash and cash equivalents divided by Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months (the adjustments for which are discussed above in connection with Adjusted EBITDA) adjusted for certain items as provided in Post's credit agreement. Post believes this measure is useful to investors in determining Post's debt levels and ability to service debt.

Consolidated interest coverage ratio as calculated under Post's credit agreement
Consolidated interest coverage ratio as calculated under Post's credit agreement is a non-GAAP measure which represents Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months adjusted for certain items as provided in Post's credit agreement (which reflects the adjustments for Adjusted EBITDA discussed under the Net leverage as calculated under Post's credit agreement section above) divided by interest expense, net for the last twelve months. Post believes this measure is useful to investors in determining Post's ability to service debt.

LOS ANGELES, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Today, eXoZymes Inc. (NASDAQ:EXOZ) ("eXoZymes") - a pioneer of AI-enhanced enzymes that transform abundant feedstock into valuable nutraceuticals and novel medicines - will host an investor webinar at 5:00 PM Eastern Time to discuss results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provide an update on recent business developments.

Michael Heltzen, CEO of eXoZymes, states, "We're entering an exciting new phase for eXoZymes as we advance our lead product toward commercial manufacturing while expanding our pipeline of high-value molecules. Our progress with Curia and the advancement of additional product candidates demonstrate how we intend to turn our technology into a repeatable engine for commercial opportunities. We believe our ability to move rapidly from discovery toward scalable production is what sets our platform apart."

Third quarter highlights

  • Commercial manufacturing preparations underway with Curia: In September, eXoZymes selected Curia as its commercial-scale manufacturing partner for NCT, the rare natural molecule behind its lead supplement brand, Tyferyn. Technology transfer began in the fourth quarter of 2026, with the collaboration intended to support larger-scale manufacturing in 2027, representing an important step toward commercial readiness.
  • Tyferyn introduced as the brand for human use: eXoZymes introduced Tyferyn as the new brand name for its lead nutraceutical ingredient focused on human wellness applications. The rebranding establishes a distinctive, consumer-friendly identity as the Company advances preparations for commercialization.
  • Product pipeline expands: eXoZymes has advanced two additional supplement candidates through proof of concept, demonstrating the broader potential of its cell-free biomanufacturing platform. Product SAPPHIRE, targeting joint comfort, has begun scale-up activities, while Product AMETHYST, targeting mental stress, focus and energy, has also completed proof of concept. The programs support the Company's strategy of building a diversified portfolio of high-value products using its shared enzyme technology and development capabilities.
  • Operational and financial update: Operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $3.05 million, compared with $2.52 million for the same period in 2025. Net loss was $2.24 million for the quarter and $7.49 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Net loss for the quarter includes a $0.77 million non-cash gain from the change in fair value of warrant liabilities. The Company ended the quarter with $3.26 million in cash and cash equivalents, which the Company expects will support operations through the beginning of 2027.

Investors and interested parties can access the live webinar through eXoZymes' investor relations website at:
https://video.exozymes.com/exoz-investor-update-3q26-nov-19

Michael Heltzen, CEO of eXoZymes, will lead the call and be joined by select members of the management team to review recent developments and ongoing initiatives. A recording and transcript of the conference call will also be made publicly available following the event.

About eXoZymes
Founded in 2019, eXoZymes is pioneering a cell-free biomanufacturing platform that uses AI-enhanced enzymes - called exozymes - to make valuable natural products and new analogs outside living cells. The company's platform is designed to replace inefficient extraction and petrochemical processes with a scalable way to produce high-value molecules for nutraceutical and pharmaceutical markets.

eXoZymes is building a portfolio of biosolutions across NCT - now Tyferyn for human use - cannabinoid analogs, santalene, and other high-value natural product molecules, with potential commercialization paths that include partnerships, licensing and joint ventures. Learn more at exozymes.com

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Kidoz Inc. (TSXV:KDOZ)(OTCQB:KDOZF), a full-stack global advertising platform powered by contextual AI, enabling brand performance without the reliance on personal data, today announced its unaudited condensed interim financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are presented in United States dollars and are in accordance with United States Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.

Kidoz generated revenue of $9.90 million for the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 12% over the same period in 2025 and the highest nine-month revenue in the Company's history. Third-quarter revenue was $3.62 million, up 9% from the second quarter of 2026 and 1% below the record $3.67 million reported in Q3 2025. Gross profit increased reflecting a stronger revenue mix and improved publisher economics, whilst higher operating expenditures reflected continued investment across sales and marketing, content and software development, compensation, and organizational capacity.

Q3 2026 Financial Result Summary

  • Total Revenue of $3,619,174, a decrease of 1% compared with $3,666,521 in Q3 2025, and an increase of 9% compared with $3,334,835 in Q2 2026.
  • Sales and Marketing expenditure of $653,103, an increase of 93% from $339,217 in Q3 2025.
  • Content and Software Development expenditure of $901,248, a decrease of 12% from $1,024,944 in Q3 2025.
  • Operating expenses of $2,189,897, an increase of 23% from $1,780,533 in Q3 2025, including a provision for doubtful receivables of $159,349 (Q3 2025 - $16,949).
  • Net loss and comprehensive loss of ($555,124), compared with ($177,711) in Q3 2025 and ($1,558,343) in Q2 2026.

Nine Months 2026 Financial Result Summary

  • Total Revenue of $9,900,750, an increase of 12% compared with $8,835,040 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Sales and Marketing expenditure of $1,945,031, an increase of 76% from $1,104,001.
  • Content and Software Development expenditure of $2,730,142, an increase of 8% from $2,516,624.
  • Operating expenses of $7,203,020, an increase of 32% from $5,467,178, including annual bonuses and incentive compensation of $862,864 recognized in Q2 2026 (2025 - $687,728).
  • Net loss and comprehensive loss of ($2,928,031), compared with ($1,289,051) for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Cash of $617,730 and working capital of $2,422,886 as at September 30, 2026, compared with cash of $1,790,483 and working capital of $3,204,557 as at September 30, 2025, and cash of $4,454,295 and working capital of $5,080,637 as at December 31, 2025.
  • Cash used in operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 of ($3,833,512), including a $2,341,317 reduction in accounts payable and accrued liabilities, compared with cash used in operating activities of ($972,758) for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Current ratio of 2.10 as at September 30, 2026, compared with 2.15 as at September 30, 2025.

"Kidoz has generated $9.9 million in revenue through the first nine months of 2026, a 12% increase and the strongest nine-month performance in our history," said Jason Williams, Kidoz CEO. "Third-quarter revenue grew 9% from the second quarter, and total revenue was essentially flat against a record Q3 last year."

"Our third-quarter loss of $0.56 million was well below the second quarter, which carried our annual performance bonuses. We continued to invest in sales and marketing to broaden our brand and agency relationships, while content and software development costs came down 12% year over year. The quarter also includes a $159,349 provision for doubtful receivables, largely related to a single customer that ceased operations."

"As in prior years, a significant proportion of our annual revenue has historically been generated in the fourth quarter, while investments in technology, sales and people are made throughout the year. This is not guidance for any future period, but it is important context for our quarterly results. We remain focused on disciplined capital deployment while building the capabilities that support durable, long-term growth for shareholders."

Additional Financial Information

The Company's financial statements note that, in the second and third quarter of 2026, certain server costs were reclassified from content and software development to cost of sales, and bonuses and incentive compensation were reclassified from several operating expense categories to a separate bonus and incentive compensation line. These reclassifications changed the presentation of cost of sales, gross profit and individual operating expense line items in the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive Loss, but had no impact on loss from operations, net loss, loss per share, the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets, the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Stockholders' Equity or the Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flow. Comparative 2025 results were recast for presentation purposes.

For full details of the Company's operations and financial results, please refer to the Securities and Exchange Commission website at www.sec.gov, the Kidoz Inc. investor website at https://investor.kidoz.net, or the SEDAR+ website at https://www.sedarplus.ca.

About Kidoz Inc.

Kidoz Inc. (TSXV:KDOZ)(OTCQB:KDOZF) (www.kidoz.net) is a full-stack global advertising platform powered by contextual AI, enabling brand performance in mobile games without personal data.

Originally developed for children's digital environments, where compliance and safety requirements are among the highest, Kidoz delivers privacy-first advertising without reliance on personal data tracking or behavioural profiling. Its technology combines proprietary SDK integrations, the Kidoz Privacy Shield, and the Kite IQ contextual AI engine to match advertising to content, environment, and geography, in alignment with COPPA, GDPR-K, Apple ATT, and global standards.

The platform supports both children's and all-ages audiences through its Kidoz and Prado offerings, enabling brands to scale performance across the global mobile gaming ecosystem using safe, trusted, contextual, privacy-first targeting.

Google-certified and Apple-approved, Kidoz reaches a global audience across mobile apps and games and is trusted by leading global brands.
